question: is there an art major at ramapo or just a minor
answer:

question: what classes do you need for the biology major
answer:
The catalog lists the Biology BS (Bachelor of Science); Biology Minor is also published. [15]

Required major courses: BIOL 111 & 111L; BIOL 113 & 113L; BIOL 332 & 332L; BIOL 356; BIOL 407 & 407L; CHEM 117 & 117L; PHYS 111 & 118L; PHYS 113 & 119L. Organic chemistry: choose one option—CHEM 206 & 206L, or CHEM 211 & 211L plus CHEM 213 & 213L. Ecology: choose BIOL 221 or ENSC 220. Math: choose 2—CMPS 147, BIOL 354 or PSYC 242, MATH 110, 121 or 122. [1]

Choose 4 electives, including at least 1 with lab/field and at least 1 without lab/field. Lab/field options: BIOL 214/214L & 216/216L; 311/311L; 320; 324; 328/328L; 349; 410/410L; 420; 430; ENSC 220/220L, 320 or 417/417L. No-lab/field options: BIIN 350, 351; BIOL 204, 304, 335, 343, 345, 346, 347, 354, 357, 390; CHEM 425; GEOG 309; ENSC 320. Also required: PATH 001, 002 and 003. [1]

BIOL 113 is 4 credits; BIOL 113L is 1 credit. Each requires BIOL 110, or BIOL 111 and 111L; take BIOL 113L concurrently with 113 and 113 concurrently with 113L. [2][3]

question: does ramapo have anything like scientific illustration or a major that combines art and science
answer:
Ramapo lists no Scientific Illustration major in its catalog. It does offer COMM 224 FUNDAMENTALS OF ILLUSTRATION (4 credits; no published prerequisites). The catalog describes it as investigating “illustration’s capacity for personal expression within the arena of public communication,” including picture building, conceptual development, materials, and professional sharing and feedback. COMM 224 is not listed in the Visual Arts BA requirements. [2][1][5]

The catalog lists a Visual Arts BA and an Interdisciplinary Studies BA, but no specifically named art-and-science major. [5] A related option is the Visual Arts BA’s joint Art Therapy degree option: students complete the BA at Ramapo, then continue at Caldwell University for an MA in Counseling with Mental Health Counseling/Art Therapy Specialization. It combines visual arts with psychology coursework, rather than being a scientific-illustration program. [1][7]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-ARTS) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/COMM224) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/freshmen/admission-requirements/)

question: what is intro to drawing about and how many credits is it
answer:
ARTS 101 Fundamentals of Drawing introduces the conceptual and perceptual bases of drawing. It addresses formal two-dimensional problems—line, tone, organization, space, shape, light, rhythm movement, and volume—using traditional and contemporary drawing techniques. A course fee is required. It is 4 credits and has no published prerequisites. [1]

question: does an art class count for gen ed or do i need a specific category
answer:
You need a course approved for a specific General Education category; being an art class alone does not establish that it counts. The pages say to choose two of the three distribution categories, and to check the catalog’s approved General Education courses. [6][7][8]
Examples of art courses with Gen Ed attributes in the catalog: ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 209 3D MODELING AND ANIMATION, and ARTS 214 BASIC CERAMICS are Culture & Creativity; ARTS 217 LOCAL TO GLOBAL: WORLD ANIMATION NOW and ARTS 230 REVOLUTION & LIGHT: THE ROOTS OF HAITIAN ART are Global Awareness; ARTS 219 ART AND INTERACTION is Values and Ethics. [3]
The curriculum page says take one course in two of three distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics; at least one must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. [8] See the approved courses in the catalog: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses. [7]

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/)

question: what are the gen ed requirements i need to finish regardless of major
answer:
Ramapo students complete ten General Education courses: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories. [3]

Keystone courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Critical Reading & Writing 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits. [3] Another catalog page calls this course Critical Reading and Writing II. [4][9] It says reading and writing, as well as mathematics, must be completed by 64 earned credits; Banner blocks registration until Critical Reading and Writing II and general education mathematics are completed. [9]

Keystone categories: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits. [3]

Distribution: take one course in two of three categories. Page [3] lists Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics; page [6] lists Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society, so the pages differ in the category names. Page [3] says at least one course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major. Page [6] says that starting Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools. [3][6]

Approved General Education courses: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses [8]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education-reading-writing-and-mathematics)

question: whats the order for the chem classes in the biochem major, like which one comes first
answer:
The catalog lists the major as Biochemistry BS [15]. In its recommended plan for students admitted in 2026–2027, the first chemistry course is CHEM 116, in First Year, Fall (18 credits). The chemistry sequence shown is: First Year, Spring—CHEM 117 (18 credits); Second Year, Fall—CHEM 211 and CHEM 211L (18 credits); Second Year, Spring—CHEM 213 and CHEM 213L (18 credits); Third Year, Fall—CHEM 324 and CHEM 324L, plus CHEM 425 (15.5 credits); Third Year, Spring—CHEM 350, CHEM 446, and CHEM 430 (16 credits); Fourth Year, Fall—CHEM 350L (14.5 credits). Fourth Year, Spring is 15.5 credits; the plan lists no chemistry course there. [1]

CHEM 425 is required for the major. Its prerequisites are BIOL 332 and either (CHEM 205) or (CHEM 206 and CHEM 206L), plus one of CHEM 212 or CHEM 213 and CHEM 213L. [1][3] The plan lists CHEM 425 in the same semester as BIOL 332; the prerequisites specify BIOL 332 as a prerequisite. [1][3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BCHM) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CHEM425) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: can a lab science class count for both gen ed and a minor at the same time
answer:
Yes. General Education courses may double count toward a minor, up to two courses [4]. For example, GEOL 106 Fundamentals of Earth Science Lecture and GEOL 106L Fundamentals of Earth Science Lab each count for General Education Scientific Reasoning [3], and both are required for the Earth Science Minor [1]. The policy does not exclude lab science from this Gen Ed/minor double-counting allowance; its lab-science exclusion concerns credits counted toward a minor’s 16–24-credit total [5]. Check with the Office of the Provost (provost@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7330; first floor of the Birch Mansion) about applying this to your specific course and minor [4].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-ERTH) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)
